   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.

   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622

   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state.    651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here. First, they state that the robustness of the Magic Square self-test is $O(\eps)$; however they specify the closeness between the actual and ideal states in terms of the trace norm, whereas we specify the closeness between $\phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}\otimes \ket{\aux}$ in terms of the Euclidean distance, which translates to $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ instead of $O(\eps)$.     68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if

    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}

    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using

    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.

    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}

   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.
   104	Using Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}) we can assume
   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$

   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes
   112	    \C_{\alice'}^d) \otimes (\C_\bob^2 \otimes \C_{\bob'}^d)\;,

   114	  where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ is obtained from $\ket{\psi}$ by permuting the two
   115	  players' registers.
   116	  Observe that $\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under permutation of $\alice\alice'$
   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.

   120	  acting on the Hilbert space $\C^2 \otimes \C^d$ as follows:

   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let

   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}

   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$.

   217	We introduce several distance measures that are used throughout.

   219	\begin{definition}[Distance between states]
   220	  \label{def:state-distance}
   221	
   222		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ be two
   223	  families of states in the same space $\mH$.
   224	  For some function $\delta : \N \to [0,1]$ we say that $\{ \ket{\psi_n} \}$ and
   225	  $\{ \ket{\psi'_n} \}$ are \emph{$\delta$-close}, denoted as $\ket{\psi}
   226	  \approx_\delta \ket{\psi'}$, if $ \norm{\ket{\psi_n} - \ket{\psi'_n}}^2 =
   227	  O(\delta(n))$.
   228	  (For convenience we generally leave the dependence of the states and $\delta$
   229	  on the indexing parameter $n$ implicit, writing e.g.\ $\ket{\psi}$ for $\ket{\psi_n}$.)

   232	\begin{definition}[Consistency between POVMs]
   233	  \label{def:consistency}
   234		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$.
   235	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}_A \otimes \cal{H}_B$ be a quantum state, and for
   236	  all $x\in \mX$, $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ POVMs.
   237	  We write
   238	  \begin{equation*}
   239	    A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \simeq_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a
   240	  \end{equation*}
   241	  on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ if
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_{a\ne b} \bra{\psi} A^x_a \otimes B^x_b \ket{\psi}
   244	    = O(\delta)\;.\footnote{Here the use of the $O(\cdot)$ notation refers to the fact that the notation will often be used to measure consistency for \emph{famillies} of POVM and states indexed by an implicit parameter $n\in \mathbb{N}$, which will always be clear from context but omitted for legibility, see Definition~\ref{def:state-distance}. The $O(\cdot)$ is taken as $n\to\infty$.}
   245	  \end{equation*}
   246	  In this case, we say that $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are
   247	  \emph{$\delta$-consistent} on $\ket{\psi}$.
   248	\end{definition}

   250	Note that a consistent measurement on $\ket{\psi}$ according to
   251	Definition~\ref{def:consistent-measurement} is $0$-consistent with itself on the same $\ket{\psi}$ and under
   252	the singleton distribution, according to Definition~\ref{def:consistency} (and
   253	vice-versa). This is because 
   254	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} =1 \,\implies \, \forall a\;,\;\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi} = M_a \otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\;,\]

   256	\[ 1 = \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\, \leq\, \Big(\sum_a \|\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\|^2 \Big)\Big(\sum_a \|M_a\otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\|^2 \Big)^{1/2} \,\leq\,1 \;.\]

   258	\begin{definition}[Distance between POVMs]
   259	  \label{def:povm-distance}
   260		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$. 
   261	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}$ be a quantum state, and for all $x\in \mX$,
   262	  $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ two POVMs on $\mH$.
   263	  We say that \emph{$\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are $\delta$-close on state
   264	    $\ket{\psi}$ and under distribution $\mu$} if
   265	  \begin{equation*}
   266	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_a \norm{ (M^x_a - N^x_a) \ket{\psi} }^2 \leq O(\delta)\;,
   267	  \end{equation*}
   268	  and we write $M^x_a \approx_\delta N^x_a$ to denote this when the state
   269	  $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ are clear from context.
   270	  This distance is referred to as the \emph{state-dependent} distance.

   273	\begin{definition}[Distance between strategies]
   274	  \label{def:strategy-distance}
   275	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a nonlocal game
   276	  and let $\strategy = (\psi, A, B)$, $\strategy' = (\psi', A', B')$ be 
   277	  strategies for $\game$.
   278	  For $\delta\in[0,1]$ we say that \emph{$\strategy$ is $\delta$-close to
   279	    $\strategy'$} if the following conditions hold.
   280	  \begin{enumerate}
   281		\item The states $\ket{\psi}, \ket{\psi'}$ are states in the same
   282	    Hilbert space $\mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ and are $\delta$-close.
   283		\item For all $x \in \cal{X}, y \in \cal{Y}$, we have $A^x_a \approx_\delta
   284	    (A')^x_a$ and $B^y_b \approx_\delta (B')^y_b$, with the approximations
   285	    holding under the distribution $\mu$, and on either $\ket{\psi}$ or
   286	    $\ket{\psi'}$.

     4	/-!
     5	# The Magic Square game
     6	
     7	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     8	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
     9	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    10	carrier is needed here.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    24	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    26	-/
    27	inductive MsType where
    28	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    29	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    30	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    31	
    32	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    33	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    34	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    35	-/
    36	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    37	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    38	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    39	
    40	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    41	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    42	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    43	-/
    44	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    45	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    46	
    47	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    48	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    50	-/
    51	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    52	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    53	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    54	
    55	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    56	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    57	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    58	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    59	-/
    60	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    61	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    62	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    63	
    64	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    65	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    66	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    67	-/
    68	inductive MsAnswer where
    69	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    70	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    71	  deriving DecidableEq
    72	
    73	/-- A formalization-only total relabeling from the global Magic Square answer
    74	alphabet to a bit. It folds wrong-form answers into zero so that a variable
    75	question yields a complete binary measurement. -/
    76	def msBitOrZero : MsAnswer → ZMod 2
    77	  | .bit b => b
    78	  | .triple _ => 0
    79	
    80	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    81	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    82	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    84	-/
    85	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    86	
    87	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    88	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    89	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    91	-/
    92	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    93	  toFun
    94	    | .triple β => .inl β
    95	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    96	  invFun
    97	    | .inl β => .triple β
    98	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    99	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   100	  right_inv := by
   101	    intro x
   102	    cases x <;> rfl
   103	
   104	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
   105	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
   106	
   107	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
   108	
   109	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   110	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   112	-/
   113	def msWinPredicate :
   114	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   115	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   116	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   117	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   118	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   119	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   120	      decide
   121	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   122	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   123	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   124	      decide
   125	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   126	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   127	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   128	
   129	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   130	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   132	-/
   133	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   134	  QuestionA := MsType
   135	  QuestionB := MsType
   136	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   137	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   138	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   139	  μ_prob := by sorry
   140	  decide := msWinPredicate

     3	/-!
     4	# Finite-field bases and the fixed binary representation
     5	
     6	The Pauli basis test uses fields of size `2^k` for odd `k`, together with a
     7	chosen self-dual normal basis over `ZMod 2`.  This file records that choice as
     8	data, while exposing Mathlib's basis and algebra-trace APIs for later proofs.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The declarations correspond to `def:admissible-size`, `def:subfields-kappa`,
    13	`def:subfield-trace`, and `def:binary-representation` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:182-232` and `298-315`.
    15	Their paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:433-502,653-728`.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	/-- `IsAdmissibleSize q` is the predicate `q = 2^k` for an odd exponent.
    23	This is `def:admissible-size` in the blueprint
    24	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:210-212`, with paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:662-667`.
    26	-/
    27	def IsAdmissibleSize (q : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ k : ℕ, Odd k ∧ q = 2 ^ k
    28	
    29	/--
    30	A fixed finite-field model records the carrier and the chosen coding of its
    31	elements by `Fin q`.  The algebra structure and stored basis data make explicit
    32	the paper's once-and-for-all self-dual normal-basis convention; they are
    33	deliberately part of the model rather than quantified afresh by the soundness
    34	theorem.  This is the Lean carrier for `def:binary-representation`, blueprint
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`, paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-728`.
    37	-/
    38	/- The finite-field carrier is specialized to `Type 0`, as are the finite
    39	models used by the surrounding Euclidean-space API. -/
    40	structure FixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) extends MIPStarRE.LDT.FieldModel.{0} q where
    41	  /-- Scalar restriction from `ZMod 2` to the chosen field. -/
    42	  algebra : Algebra (ZMod 2) K
    43	  /-- Dimension of the chosen basis over the prime subfield. -/
    44	  basisDim : ℕ
    45	  /-- The chosen basis dimension is odd, as required for a self-dual normal basis
    46	  over the binary field. -/
    47	  basisDimOdd : Odd basisDim
    48	  /-- The admissible field-size relation for the chosen basis dimension. -/
    49	  basisCard : q = 2 ^ basisDim
    50	  /-- The chosen basis of `K` over `ZMod 2`. -/
    51	  basis : Module.Basis (Fin basisDim) (ZMod 2) K
    52	  /--
    53	  The inherited coding of `K` is the natural binary encoding of the stored
    54	  basis coordinates.  This field records the source's `downsize` convention
    55	  rather than allowing an unrelated permutation of `Fin q`.  It is the
    56	  coordinate clause of `def:binary-representation` in
    57	  `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`, with paper origin
    58	  `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:669-680`.
    59	  -/
    60	  representation_natural :
    61	    ∀ v : Fin basisDim → ZMod 2,
    62	      (toFieldModel.equiv (basis.equivFun.symm v)).val =
    63	        ∑ i : Fin basisDim, if v i = 1 then 2 ^ i.1 else 0
    64	  /-- Self-duality of the chosen basis with respect to the field trace. -/
    65	  selfDual : ∀ i j, Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (basis i * basis j) =
    66	    if i = j then 1 else 0
    67	  /-- Normality of the chosen basis, recorded by a Frobenius generator. -/
    68	  normal : ∃ α : K, ∀ i, basis i = α ^ (2 ^ i.1)
    69	
    70	/-!
    71	The paper fixes the field representation and self-dual normal basis once for
    72	each admissible field size.  We expose that choice through a single global
    73	selector rather than carrying a potentially different model in every game
    74	parameter record.  Existence is a named stage-4.3 proof obligation; the
    75	selector itself is the resulting noncomputable choice.
    76	-/
    77	
    78	/-- An admissible binary field size admits the fixed self-dual normal model used
    79	by the Pauli basis test.  This is the existence assertion implicit in
    80	`def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis` and `def:binary-representation`, blueprint
    81	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:234-246,298-315`, paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680,702-725`.
    83	
    84	The construction of the basis and its natural coding is deferred to the
    85	algebra stage; keeping it as a named theorem makes the proof obligation visible
    86	without adding a model hypothesis to the source-facing test statements.
    87	-/
    88	theorem exists_fixed_field_model (q : ℕ) (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) :
    89	    Nonempty (FixedFieldModel q) := by
    90	  sorry
    91	
    92	/-- The once-and-for-all field model selected for an admissible size.  Every
    93	QPBT parameter record uses this same choice, matching the paper's fixed
    94	self-dual normal-basis identification rather than quantifying over arbitrary
    95	representations.  Blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`; paper origin
    96	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680`.
    97	-/
    98	noncomputable def fixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) :
    99	    FixedFieldModel q :=
   100	  Classical.choice (exists_fixed_field_model q hq)
   101	
   102	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Field F.K := F.toFieldModel.instField
   103	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Fintype F.K := F.toFieldModel.instFintype
   104	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : DecidableEq F.K := F.toFieldModel.instDecidableEq
   105	instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Algebra (ZMod 2) F.K := F.algebra
   106	
   107	/-- The fixed binary representation obtained from the chosen basis coordinates. -/
   108	noncomputable def binaryRepresentation {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : F.K ≃ Fin q :=
   109	  F.toFieldModel.equiv
   110	
   111	/--
   112	The coordinate map associated with a finite basis.  This is the `κ` of
   113	`def:subfields-kappa` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:182-208`,
   114	whose paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:433-502`.
   115	-/
   116	noncomputable abbrev kappa {F K ι : Type*} [CommSemiring F] [Semiring K]
   117	    [Algebra F K] [Finite ι]
   118	    (b : Module.Basis ι F K) : K ≃ₗ[F] (ι → F) :=
   119	  b.equivFun
   120	
   121	/--
   122	Multiplication by `a` in basis coordinates, using Mathlib's
   123	`Algebra.leftMulMatrix`.  It is the multiplication table `K_a` in
   124	`def:subfields-kappa` (blueprint lines 196-199; paper
   125	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`).
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable abbrev multiplicationTable {F K ι : Type*} [CommSemiring F]
   128	    [Semiring K] [Algebra F K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   129	    (b : Module.Basis ι F K) : K →ₐ[F] Matrix ι ι F :=
   130	  Algebra.leftMulMatrix b
   131	
   132	/--
   133	The finite-field trace used by the Pauli phases.  This is a thin wrapper around
   134	Mathlib's basis-independent `Algebra.trace`, matching `def:subfield-trace` and
   135	Equation `eq:def-trace` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:217-232`
   136	(`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`).
   137	-/
   138	noncomputable abbrev binTrace (K : Type*) [CommRing K] [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] :
   139	    K →ₗ[ZMod 2] ZMod 2 :=
   140	  Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K
   141	
   142	/-- The trace selected by a fixed model; this is the map denoted `tr` in the
   143	paper's `def:binary-representation`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`,
   144	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680`. -/
   145	noncomputable def fixedBinTrace {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : F.K → ZMod 2 :=
   146	  binTrace F.K
   147	
   148	/--
   149	The matrix-trace presentation of `fixedBinTrace`, a statement-level bridge to
   150	Equation `eq:def-trace`.  It is the trace assertion in `def:subfield-trace`,
   151	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:217-232`, paper origin
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`.  Mathlib's
   153	`Algebra.trace_eq_matrix_trace` supplies the basis-independent equality.
   154	-/
   155	theorem fixedBinTrace_eq_matrixTrace {q ι : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q)
   156	    (b : Module.Basis (Fin ι) (ZMod 2) F.K) (a : F.K) :
   157	    fixedBinTrace F a = (multiplicationTable b a).trace := by
   158	  exact Algebra.trace_eq_matrix_trace b a
   159	
   160	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    30	/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter package.  Its scalar carrier
    31	uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
    32	self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
    33	is `def:admissible` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    36	-/
    37	structure AdmissibleParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    42	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    43	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    44	
    45	/-- The positivity of the ambient dimension is a proof obligation implicit in
    46	the admissibility convention `def:admissible`, blueprint
    47	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
    48	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    49	-/
    50	theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
    51	  sorry
    52	
    53	/-- The fixed model accessor for an admissible parameter package.  It is a
    54	compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
    55	quantified field representation.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`; paper
    56	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    57	-/
    58	noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model (P : AdmissibleParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    59	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    60	
    61	/-- The low-degree parameter view of an admissible Pauli-test package.  This is
    62	a Lean-only bridge supporting the statement closure; it is not an additional
    63	hypothesis of `thm:pauli`.  Blueprint
    64	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    65	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    66	-/
    67	def AdmissibleParams.toLdParams (P : AdmissibleParams) : LdParams where
    68	  q := P.q
    69	  m := P.m
    70	  d := P.d
    71	  k := 1
    72	  hm := P.one_le_m
    73	  hd := P.hd
    74	  hk := by decide
    75	  hq := P.hq
    76	  hdvd := P.hdvd

    83	-/

item.text: Several proposals are genuine source-coverage gaps, but they are not equally urgent.      5	/-!
     6	# Distribution infrastructure for the low individual degree test
     7	
     8	Shared distribution definitions: finite-support weighted distributions,
     9	a probability predicate, push-forward distributions, weighted-sum linear maps,
    10	averaging, uniform distribution, and outcome summation.
    11	
    12	Note: this module contributes declarations to the comparator statement closure
    13	of `mainFormal`, which must elaborate in the same environment as the
    14	Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  Keep the full `import Mathlib`; do not narrow
    15	it.  See `docs/comparator.md`, "Environment alignment".
    16	-/

    18	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

    20	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    21	
    22	/-- A finite-support weighted distribution with nonnegative real-valued weights. -/
    23	structure Distribution (α : Type*) where
    24	  support : Finset α := ∅
    25	  weight : α → Error := fun _ => 0
    26	  nonnegative : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a := by intro _; positivity
    27	  outsideSupport : ∀ a, a ∉ support → weight a = 0 := by intro _ _; rfl
    28	
    29	namespace Distribution
    30	
    31	/-- The total mass carried by the explicit support of a distribution. -/
    32	def totalWeight {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Error :=
    33	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a
    34	
    35	/-- A `Distribution` is probabilistic when its total mass is exactly `1`. -/
    36	def IsProbability {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Prop :=
    37	  𝒟.totalWeight = 1
    38	
    39	/-- Push a finite-support distribution forward along a map.
    40	
    41	This is the project `Distribution` analogue of `PMF.map`.  The support is the
    42	image of the original finite support, and each new weight is the sum of the
    43	weights in the corresponding fiber. -/
    44	noncomputable def map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    45	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) : Distribution β where
    46	  support := 𝒟.support.image e
    47	  weight := fun b => ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a
    48	  nonnegative := fun _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a
    49	  outsideSupport := fun _ hb =>
    50	    Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha =>
    51	      (hb (Finset.mem_image.mpr
    52	        ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩)).elim
    53	
    54	@[simp]
    55	theorem map_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    56	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    57	    (𝒟.map e).support = 𝒟.support.image e := rfl
    58	
    59	@[simp]
    60	theorem map_weight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    61	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (b : β) :
    62	    (𝒟.map e).weight b =
    63	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a := rfl
    64	
    65	/-- Push-forward preserves total mass. -/
    66	theorem map_totalWeight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    67	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    68	    (𝒟.map e).totalWeight = 𝒟.totalWeight := by
    69	  simpa [totalWeight, map] using
    70	    (Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    71	      (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    72	      (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩) 𝒟.weight)
    73	
    74	/-- A finite weighted sum over a push-forward distribution is the corresponding
    75	weighted sum of the pulled-back family.  This is the `Distribution` analogue of
    76	the finite-sum form of `PMF.map`. -/
    77	theorem map_sum_smul {α β M : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    78	    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    79	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → M) :
    80	    ∑ b ∈ (𝒟.map e).support, (𝒟.map e).weight b • f b =
    81	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    82	  classical
    83	  calc
    84	    ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    85	        (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a) • f b
    86	        = ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    87	            ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    88	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    89	          intro b _
    90	          rw [Finset.sum_smul]
    91	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    92	          intro a ha
    93	          exact congrArg (fun x => 𝒟.weight a • f x) (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2.symm
    94	    _ = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    95	          exact Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    96	            (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    97	            (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩)
    98	            (fun a => 𝒟.weight a • f (e a))
    99	
   100	end Distribution
   101	
   102	/-- On a finite ambient type, a summand that vanishes outside a distribution's
   103	explicit support has the same total sum over all ambient values as over that support.
   104	
   105	This is a project-local explicit-support adapter around Mathlib's `Finset.sum_subset`:
   106	Mathlib supplies the finite-sum theorem, while this lemma packages the common shape used
   107	when paper expressions sum over a whole question set but the repository stores a smaller
   108	`Distribution.support`.  It is not intended to replace Mathlib probability theory. -/
   109	theorem Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support {α β : Type*} [Fintype α]
   110	    [AddCommMonoid β] (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → β)
   111	    (hf : ∀ a, a ∉ 𝒟.support → f a = 0) :
   112	    (∑ a : α, f a) = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, f a := by
   113	  classical
   114	  simpa using
   115	    (Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ 𝒟.support)
   116	      (fun a _ ha => hf a ha)).symm
   117	
   118	namespace Distribution.IsProbability
   119	
   120	/-- Unpack the equality form of the probability invariant. -/
   121	theorem weight_sum_eq_one {α : Type*}
   122	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   123	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a = 1 := by
   124	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight] using h𝒟
   125	
   126	/-- On a finite ambient type, a probabilistic `Distribution` has total weight `1` even
   127	when its weights are summed over the whole ambient type.
   128	
   129	This packages the explicit-support bookkeeping in `Distribution` for downstream Lean
   130	statements that follow the paper's notation `𝔼_{x ∼ 𝒟}` over the question set rather
   131	than over a stored support finset. -/
   132	theorem weight_sum_univ_eq_one {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
   133	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   134	    (∑ a : α, 𝒟.weight a) = 1 := by
   135	  rw [Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support 𝒟 𝒟.weight 𝒟.outsideSupport]
   136	  exact h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one
   137	
   138	/-- A probability distribution has total weight at most `1`. -/
   139	theorem weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*}
   140	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   141	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a ≤ 1 :=
   142	  le_of_eq h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one
   143	
   144	/-- Push-forward preserves the probability invariant. -/
   145	theorem map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   146	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
   147	    (𝒟.map e).IsProbability := by
   148	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.map_totalWeight] using h𝒟
   149	
   150	end Distribution.IsProbability
   151	
   152	namespace Distribution
   153	
   154	/-- The Mathlib probability mass function associated to a project `Distribution`
   155	whose total mass is one.
   156	
   157	The construction sends each nonnegative real weight to `ℝ≥0∞` by
   158	`ENNReal.ofReal`; the hypotheses of `PMF.ofFinset` are exactly the project
   159	probability invariant and the stored zero-off-support condition. -/
   160	noncomputable def toPMF {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   161	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) : PMF α :=
   162	  PMF.ofFinset (fun a => ENNReal.ofReal (𝒟.weight a)) 𝒟.support
   163	    (by
   164	      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a),
   165	        h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one]
   166	      simp)
   167	    (by
   168	      intro a ha
   169	      rw [𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
   170	      simp)
   171	
   172	@[simp]
   173	theorem toPMF_apply {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   174	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (a : α) :
   175	    𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a = ENNReal.ofReal (𝒟.weight a) := rfl
   176	
   177	@[simp]
   178	theorem toPMF_apply_toReal {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   179	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (a : α) :
   180	    (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal = 𝒟.weight a := by
   181	  rw [toPMF_apply, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (𝒟.nonnegative a)]
   182	
   183	/-- The associated PMF has zero mass outside the stored support of the project
   184	distribution. -/
   185	theorem toPMF_apply_of_notMem {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   186	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) {a : α} (ha : a ∉ 𝒟.support) :
   187	    𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a = 0 := by
   188	  rw [toPMF_apply, 𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
   189	  simp
   190	
   191	/-- The project push-forward agrees with Mathlib's push-forward of the
   192	associated probability mass function. -/
   193	theorem toPMF_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   194	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
   195	    (𝒟.map e).toPMF (h𝒟.map e) = (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟).map e := by
   196	  classical
   197	  ext b
   198	  rw [toPMF_apply, PMF.map_apply, map_weight]
   199	  rw [ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg
   200	    (s := 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b))
   201	    (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a)]
   202	  rw [tsum_eq_sum (s := 𝒟.support)]
   203	  · rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   204	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   205	    intro a ha
   206	    by_cases hea : e a = b
   207	    · have hba : b = e a := hea.symm
   208	      rw [if_pos hea, if_pos hba, toPMF_apply]
   209	    · have hba : b ≠ e a := fun hba => hea hba.symm
   210	      rw [if_neg hea, if_neg hba]
   211	  · intro a ha
   212	    by_cases hba : b = e a
   213	    · rw [if_pos hba, toPMF_apply_of_notMem 𝒟 h𝒟 ha]
   214	    · rw [if_neg hba]
   215	
   216	end Distribution

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap

   367	\paragraph{Expanded state.} We introduce registers $\alice', \alice'', \bob', \bob''$ that are each isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. Define the state \begin{equation}\label{eq:def-psihat}

   369	\end{equation}
   370	where we have added maximally entangled states in registers
   371	$\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$; recall also that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is already implicitly  appended with sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the $\ket{0}$ state. 
   372	For the remainder of the Appendix all approximations will be evaluated with respect to this state.

   374	\paragraph{Expanded observables.} For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $r \in \F_q$, and $u \in \F_q^m$ define the following observable $\hat{W}^r(u)$: \begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-23}
   375		\hat{W}^r(u) = W^r(u) \otimes \tau^W(r \cdot \ind_m(u))\;,
   376	\end{equation}

   381		\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a = \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \hat{W}^r(u)\;.
   382	\]
   383	Note that $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ can be equivalently
   384	written as a sum of projectors by applying Fourier
   385	identities. Specifically, for $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $u \in \F_q^{m}$, and
   386	$a \in \F_q$, define the projector
   387	\begin{equation} \tau^{W, u}_{a} =
   388	  \tau^{W}_{[ g_{\cdot}(u) = a]} = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits}: h
   389	    \cdot \ind_m(u) = a} \tau^{W}_{h}\;. \label{eq:qld-point-obs-def} \end{equation}

   438	$\alice \alice'$ together to form  a single party, and $\bob \alice''$
   439	to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
   440	form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
   441	party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
   442	two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in

   446	derive a bipartite relation of the form

   452	  M_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} N_{\alice \bob''}, \\

   528	                drawn from the line-point distribution

   536	                drawn from the line-point distribution,

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap
   165	
   166	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

   291	
   292	The Pauli basis test is the quantum low individual degree test of Natarajan and Vidick, in the slightly modified form introduced by Natarajan and Wright~\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Informally, the test certifies that the players share the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, where $M = 2^m$. On a question of type $(\mathsf{Pauli}, W)$ with $W \in \{X,Z\}$, a player is expected to measure the generalized Pauli basis POVM $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} and report the outcome $h$. Most subtests probe limited information about $h$: given a point $u_W \in \F_q^m$, a player is expected to report the evaluation $g_h(u_W)$ of the low-degree encoding $g_h$ of $h$, and for a fixed basis $W$ these probes are checked against each other by the classical low individual degree game of Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}. Consistency \emph{between} the two bases is checked through two-outcome probes: given additionally $r_W \in \F_q$, a player reports $\tr(g_h(u_W)\, r_W) \in \F_2$.     19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/

    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)

    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,

    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)

    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/

    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=

    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/

    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=

    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/

    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA

1	# API surface for `SubMeas` obligations
     2	
     3	Focused on the declarations that help prove the usual `SubMeas` goals:
     4	
     5	- PSD / Hermitian facts
     6	- pointwise bounds such as `A.outcome a ≤ A.total` or `≤ 1`
     7	- sum identities and transport of those obligations through postprocessing / tensor placement / completion
     8	
     9	## `MIPStarRE/Quantum.lean`
    10	
    11	`Quantum.lean` itself defines no declarations. It is a re-export file:
    12	
    13	```lean
    14	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Basic
    15	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Order
    16	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.TracePairing
    17	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.BlockDiagonal
    18	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace
    19	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement
    20	```
    21	
    22	Relevant re-exported API:
    23	
    24	### From `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    25	
    26	`MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix` is now an aggregate import.  For direct
    27	dependencies, use the mathematical leaves:
    28	
    29	- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Basic`
    30	  - `Op`, trace reindexing, `Matrix.submatrixLinearMap`, and elementary
    31	    Kronecker bookkeeping.
    32	- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Order`
    33	  - positive-semidefinite order, the closed PSD cone, trace norm control,
    34	    sandwich monotonicity, `sq_le_self`, Kronecker monotonicity, and reindexing
    35	    positivity.
    36	- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.TracePairing`
    37	  - continuous real trace pairings, Hermitian representatives of continuous
    38	    real-linear functionals, weak-duality positivity, and complementary
    39	    slackness algebra.
    40	- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.BlockDiagonal`
    41	  - the linear-map form of `Matrix.blockDiagonal`, block-diagonal positivity,
    42	    and the corresponding block trace identity.
    43	- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace`
    44	  - normalized trace, `tauNormSq`, projections, and spectral truncation.
    45	
    46	- `abbrev MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d : Type*) := Matrix d d ℂ`
    47	  - The operator type used everywhere in `SubMeas`.
    48	
    49	- `def Matrix.submatrixLinearMap (R : Type*) (row : m' → m) (col : n' → n) :
    50	  Matrix m n α →ₗ[R] Matrix m' n' α`
    51	  - The linear-map form of `Matrix.submatrix`; use this for diagonal-block
    52	    projections and other coordinate restrictions instead of reproving
    53	    additivity entry by entry.
    54	
    55	- `theorem sandwich_nonneg {M P : Op d} (hP : 0 ≤ P) (hMH : Mᴴ = M) : 0 ≤ M * P * M`
    56	  - PSD is preserved under Hermitian sandwiching.
    57	
    58	- `theorem sandwich_mono {M P Q : Op d} (hMH : Mᴴ = M) (hPQ : P ≤ Q) : M * P * M ≤ M * Q * M`
    59	  - Monotonicity under sandwiching.
    60	
    61	- `theorem sq_le_self [DecidableEq d] {X : Op d} (hX : 0 ≤ X) (hXle : X ≤ 1) : X * X ≤ X`
    62	  - Standard `0 ≤ X ≤ 1` consequence.
    63	
    64	- `noncomputable def normalizedTrace (A : Op d) : ℂ`
    65	- `theorem normalizedTrace_add (A B : Op d) : normalizedTrace (A + B) = normalizedTrace A + normalizedTrace B`
    66	- `theorem normalizedTrace_sub (A B : Op d) : normalizedTrace (A - B) = normalizedTrace A - normalizedTrace B`
    67	- `theorem normalizedTrace_smul (c : ℂ) (A : Op d) : normalizedTrace (c • A) = c * normalizedTrace A`
    68	- `theorem normalizedTrace_mul_comm (A B : Op d) : normalizedTrace (A * B) = normalizedTrace (B * A)`
    69	  - Trace linearity/cyclicity tools used downstream for scalarized sum arguments.
    70	
    71	- `noncomputable def tauNormSq (A : Op d) : ℂ`
    72	- `structure IsProj (P : Op d) : Prop`
    73	- `structure SpectralTruncation (source target : Op d) : Prop`
    74	  - Less direct for basic `SubMeas` obligations, but part of the operator API.
    75	
    76	### From `MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement`
    77	
    78	- `structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]`
    79	  - Fields:
    80	    - `effect : α → Op d`
    81	    - `pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a`
    82	    - `sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1`
    83	
    84	- `structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] extends Submeasurement α d`
    85	  - Additional field:
    86	    - `sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1`
    87	
    88	- `noncomputable def Submeasurement.total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d := ∑ a, M.effect a`
    89	
    90	- `noncomputable def Submeasurement.postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d`
    91	  - Preserves PSD by fiberwise sum and preserves the `sum_le_one` obligation.

    93	## `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/SubMeasurementCore.lean` and related files
    94	
    95	The main local API for proving `SubMeas` obligations is now split across
    96	`SubMeasurementCore.lean`, `SubMeasurementFamilies.lean`, `TensorPlacement.lean`,
    97	and `MeasurementLift.lean`.
    98	
    99	### Core structures
   100	
   101	- `structure SubMeas (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]`
   102	  - Fields:
   103	    - `outcome : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι`
   104	    - `total : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι`
   105	    - `outcome_pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ outcome a`
   106	    - `sum_eq_total : ∑ a, outcome a = total`
   107	    - `total_le_one : total ≤ 1`
   108	
   109	- `structure Measurement (α : Type*) (ι : Type*) [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] extends SubMeas α ι`
   110	  - Additional field:
   111	    - `total_eq_one : total = 1`
   112	
   113	- `structure ProjSubMeas (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] extends SubMeas α ι`
   114	  - Additional field:
   115	    - `proj : ∀ a, outcome a * outcome a = outcome a`
   116	
   117	- `structure ProjMeas (α : Type*) (ι : Type*) [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] extends Measurement α ι`
   118	  - Additional field:
   119	    - `proj : ∀ a, outcome a * outcome a = outcome a`
   120	
   121	### PSD / Hermitian / bound lemmas
   122	
   123	- `theorem SubMeas.outcome_hermitian (A : SubMeas α ι) (a : α) : (A.outcome a)ᴴ = A.outcome a`
   124	
   125	- `theorem Measurement.outcome_hermitian (M : Measurement α ι) (a : α) : (M.outcome a)ᴴ = M.outcome a`
   126	
   127	- `theorem ProjSubMeas.outcome_hermitian (P : ProjSubMeas α ι) (a : α) : (P.outcome a)ᴴ = P.outcome a`
   128	
   129	- `theorem ProjMeas.outcome_hermitian (P : ProjMeas α ι) (a : α) : (P.outcome a)ᴴ = P.outcome a`
   130	
   131	- `theorem Measurement.outcome_le_one (M : Measurement α ι) (a : α) : M.outcome a ≤ 1`
   132	
   133	- `theorem SubMeas.outcome_le_total (A : SubMeas α ι) (a : α) : A.outcome a ≤ A.total`
   134	
   135	- `theorem SubMeas.outcome_le_one (A : SubMeas α ι) (a : α) : A.outcome a ≤ 1`
   136	
   137	- `theorem SubMeas.total_nonneg (A : SubMeas α ι) : 0 ≤ A.total`
   138	
   139	These are the main “obligation closers” for PSD / Hermitian / upper-bound goals.
   140	
   141	### Sum identities
   142	
   143	- `theorem Measurement.sum_eq (M : Measurement α ι) : ∑ a, M.outcome a = 1`
   144	
   145	- The defining field
   146	  - `A.sum_eq_total : ∑ a, A.outcome a = A.total`
   147	  - is the main rewrite for submeasurements.
   148	
   149	### Indexed-family transport
   150	
   151	- `abbrev IdxSubMeas (Question Outcome : Type*) (ι : Type*) := Question → SubMeas Outcome ι`
   152	- `abbrev IdxMeas (Question Outcome : Type*) (ι : Type*) := Question → Measurement Outcome ι`
   153	- `abbrev IdxProjSubMeas (Question Outcome : Type*) (ι : Type*) := Question → ProjSubMeas Outcome ι`
   154	- `abbrev IdxProjMeas (Question Outcome : Type*) (ι : Type*) := Question → ProjMeas Outcome ι`
   155	
   156	- `def IdxMeas.toIdxSubMeas (A : IdxMeas Question Outcome ι) : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι`
   157	- `def IdxProjSubMeas.toIdxSubMeas (A : IdxProjSubMeas Question Outcome ι) : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι`
   158	- `def IdxProjMeas.toIdxMeas (A : IdxProjMeas Question Outcome ι) : IdxMeas Question Outcome ι`
   159	- `def IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas (A : IdxProjMeas Question Outcome ι) : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι`
   160	
   161	These are useful when a proof wants to drop from stronger structure to plain `SubMeas`.
   162	
   163	### Constructors / transport that preserve obligations
   164	
   165	- `noncomputable def postprocess (A : SubMeas α ι) (f : α → β) : SubMeas β ι`
   166	  - New outcomes are fiberwise sums.
   167	  - Preserves:
   168	    - PSD via `Finset.sum_nonneg`
   169	    - total exactly
   170	    - `≤ 1` bound on the total
   171	
   172	- `noncomputable def completeSubMeas (A : SubMeas α ι) : Measurement (Option α) ι`
   173	  - Adds failure outcome `none ↦ 1 - A.total`.
   174	  - Standard way to turn a submeasurement into a complete measurement.
   175	
   176	- `def SubMeas.singleOutcome (A : Op ι) (hA_pos : 0 ≤ A) (hA_le_one : A ≤ 1) : SubMeas Unit ι`
   177	  - Constructs a one-outcome submeasurement from a positive operator bounded by the identity.
   178	
   179	- `def constSubMeasFamily (A : SubMeas α ι) : IdxSubMeas Unit α ι`
   180	
   181	### Tensor / placement lemmas
   182	
   183	These are the key tools when a `SubMeas` is lifted to a bipartite space.
   184	
   185	- `theorem leftTensor_finset_sum (s : Finset α) (f : α → Op ι₁) : Finset.sum s (fun a => leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) (f a)) = leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) (Finset.sum s f)`
   186	
   187	- `theorem rightTensor_finset_sum (s : Finset α) (f : α → Op ι₂) : Finset.sum s (fun a => rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (f a)) = rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (Finset.sum s f)`
   188	
   189	- `theorem leftTensor_nonneg {A : Op ι₁} (hA : 0 ≤ A) : 0 ≤ leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) A`
   190	
   191	- `theorem rightTensor_nonneg {A : Op ι₂} (hA : 0 ≤ A) : 0 ≤ rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) A`
   192	
   193	- `theorem leftTensor_le_one {A : Op ι₁} (hA : A ≤ 1) : leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) A ≤ 1`
   194	
   195	- `theorem rightTensor_le_one {A : Op ι₂} (hA : A ≤ 1) : rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) A ≤ 1`
   196	
   197	### Tensor / placement constructors
   198	
   199	- `def SubMeas.liftLeft (A : SubMeas α ι) : SubMeas α (ι × ι)`
   200	- `def IdxSubMeas.liftLeft (A : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome (ι × ι)`
   201	- `def leftPlacedSubMeas (A : SubMeas α ιA) : SubMeas α (ιA × ιB)`
   202	- `def rightPlacedSubMeas (A : SubMeas α ιB) : SubMeas α (ιA × ιB)`
   203	
   204	These package the tensor lemmas so the new `SubMeas` obligations are discharged automatically.

   206	## `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/Distribution.lean`
   207	
   208	This file is scalar-valued, not operator-valued, but it is useful for weighted sum / averaging arguments once matrix statements have been scalarized.
   209	
   210	### Core defs
   211	
   212	- `structure Distribution (α : Type*)`
   213	  - Fields:
   214	    - `support : Finset α`
   215	    - `weight : α → Error`
   216	    - `nonnegative : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a`
   217	    - `outsideSupport : ∀ a, a ∉ support → weight a = 0`
   218	
   219	- `def avgOver (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → Error) : Error := ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * f a`
   220	
   221	- `noncomputable def Distribution.weightedSumLinearMap (M : Type*) (𝒟 : Distribution α) : (α → M) →ₗ[Error] M`
   222	  - Module-valued weighted finite sum over the explicit support; use its
   223	    linearity lemmas for additive and scalar average identities.
   224	
   225	- `noncomputable def uniformDistribution (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] : Distribution α`
   226	
   227	- `noncomputable def totalVariationDistance {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (μ ν : Distribution α) : Error`
   228	  - Not directly about `SubMeas` obligations, but part of the file’s public API.

   230	### PMF adapters
   231	
   232	`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/PMFAverages.lean` contains the finite probability layer

60	\begin{remark}
    61	  Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in this paper are tensor
    62	  product strategies, and we simply call them \emph{strategies}.
    63	  Similarly, we refer to $\val^*(\game)$ as the \emph{value} of the game
    64	  $\game$.
    65	\end{remark}
    66	
    67	
    68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if
    71	  all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    72	\end{definition}
    73	
    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.
    93	
    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}
   100	
   101	\begin{proof}
   102	  By definition for any $\eps'>\eps$ there exists a strategy $\strategy'= (\ket{\psi'},A,B)$ such
   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.

   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$

   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes

   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.

   122	  	M^x_a = \ketbra{0}{0} \otimes A^x_a + \ketbra{1}{1} \otimes B^x_a \;,

   126	  question $y$, he measures $M^y$ on registers $\bob \bob'$.

   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let
   135	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\game$ such that  $\mH_A = \mH_B$.

   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}
   157	
   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$. 
   161	
   162	\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]
   163	  \label{def:consistent-strategy}
   164		Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state
   165	  $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$, for some Hilbert space~$\mH$, which is
   166	  defined on question alphabets $\cal{X}$ and~$\cal{Y}$ and answer alphabets
   167	  $\cal{A}$ and~$\cal{B}$, respectively.
   168	  We say that the strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in
   169	  \cal{X}$, the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on
   170	  $\ket{\psi}$ and if for all $y \in \cal{Y}$, the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in
   171	    \cal{B}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   172	\end{definition}
   173	
   174	We almost always restrict our attention to symmetric strategies. In this case, consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer.

The coefficients $\alpha_i$ are uniquely defined by $\ket{\psi}$ and called \emph{Schmidt coefficients}.    232	\begin{definition}[Consistency between POVMs]
   233	  \label{def:consistency}
   234		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$.
   235	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}_A \otimes \cal{H}_B$ be a quantum state, and for

The $O(\cdot)$ is taken as $n\to\infty$.}

   252	the singleton distribution, according to Definition~\ref{def:consistency} (and
   253	vice-versa). This is because 
   254	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} =1 \,\implies \, \forall a\;,\;\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi} = M_a \otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\;,\]
   255	because using that $\{M_a\}$ is a POVM there must be equality in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality

   258	\begin{definition}[Distance between POVMs]
   259	  \label{def:povm-distance}
   260		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$. 
   261	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}$ be a quantum state, and for all $x\in \mX$,
   262	  $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ two POVMs on $\mH$.
   263	  We say that \emph{$\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are $\delta$-close on state
   264	    $\ket{\psi}$ and under distribution $\mu$} if
   265	  \begin{equation*}
   266	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_a \norm{ (M^x_a - N^x_a) \ket{\psi} }^2 \leq O(\delta)\;,
   267	  \end{equation*}
   268	  and we write $M^x_a \approx_\delta N^x_a$ to denote this when the state
   269	  $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ are clear from context.
   270	  This distance is referred to as the \emph{state-dependent} distance.
   271	\end{definition}

   273	\begin{definition}[Distance between strategies]
   274	  \label{def:strategy-distance}
   275	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a nonlocal game
   276	  and let $\strategy = (\psi, A, B)$, $\strategy' = (\psi', A', B')$ be 
   277	  strategies for $\game$.
   278	  For $\delta\in[0,1]$ we say that \emph{$\strategy$ is $\delta$-close to
   279	    $\strategy'$} if the following conditions hold.
   280	  \begin{enumerate}
   281		\item The states $\ket{\psi}, \ket{\psi'}$ are states in the same
   282	    Hilbert space $\mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ and are $\delta$-close.
   283		\item For all $x \in \cal{X}, y \in \cal{Y}$, we have $A^x_a \approx_\delta
   284	    (A')^x_a$ and $B^y_b \approx_\delta (B')^y_b$, with the approximations
   285	    holding under the distribution $\mu$, and on either $\ket{\psi}$ or
   286	    $\ket{\psi'}$.
   287	  \end{enumerate}
   288	\end{definition}

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.

    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}
